result.title: VIGOR: Verifiable Industrial Geometry Optimization and Repair in Scene Programs
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate structured layouts and executable scene programs from natural-language instructions. However, executability does not imply engineering feasibility: an industrial scene program may execute successfully while its final state still violates coupled boundary, collision, clearance, aisle, or structural constraints. We identify this mismatch as the executability-engineering-feasibility gap, where locally plausible placements can remain globally infeasible because corrections to one device may introduce violations elsewhere. To make this gap measurable in a controlled setting, we construct an execution-grounded industrial scene-program dataset with 1,749 constructible scenarios, complete executable programs, and 94 final-state geometric checks per scenario. We further propose VIGOR, which combines supervised scene-program generation with execution-grounded verification and staged geometric refinement. Supervised fine-tuning establishes complete program generation, local projection resolves independently correctable violations, and joint conflict-graph repair coordinates residual multi-object conflicts while preserving structural relations. Experiments show that VIGOR achieves 96.86% Complete Feasibility and an Overall score of 91.20, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 10.42 points in Overall. These results show that, under controlled industrial layout conditions, reliable scene-program generation requires not only executable programs, but also explicit verification and coordinated resolution of coupled engineering constraints.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建了带终态几何检查的可执行工业场景程序数据集（1,749 个场景、每场景 94 项检查），并提出 VIGOR：监督式场景程序生成结合基于执行的验证与分阶段几何修正（局部投影加冲突图联合修复），以弥合「可执行」与「工程可行」之间的差距。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「执行后验证 + 局部可修与耦合冲突联合修复」的流程，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的可行性检查、耦合冲突协调与迭代修正提供方法线索，可供核查；但论文面向 LLM 场景程序生成而非多模态推理内部状态，迁移价值需人工判断。
